document_metadata.purpose: Define WHAT Reflow must do (functional capabilities) before defining HOW it does it (system architecture)

functional_requirements.requirement: Guide AI agents through structured workflows
functional_requirements.description: Provide step-by-step workflow guidance to AI agents, ensuring they execute all required steps in correct sequence without skipping critical actions
acceptance_criteria: AI agents can load and interpret workflow JSON files
Each step clearly defines actions, inputs, outputs, and next steps
Workflow steps contain sufficient context for AI agents to execute independently
Steps include validation checkpoints and quality gates

functional_requirements.requirement: Preserve workflow state across multiple sessions
functional_requirements.description: Maintain workflow progress, current step, and system context in working_memory.json to enable multi-day projects without context drift
acceptance_criteria: working_memory.json tracks current_workflow, current_step, current_substep
AI agents can resume from exact point in workflow after days/weeks
Context refresh mechanism prevents token exhaustion
Workflow state includes system name, paths, and progress summary

functional_requirements.requirement: Support multiple architectural frameworks
functional_requirements.description: Enable framework-agnostic workflow execution across IT systems, biological networks, social systems, etc. by using pluggable framework definitions
acceptance_criteria: Framework configuration selectable during setup (UAF, Systems Biology, Decision Flow, Custom)
Framework definitions specify component_term, connection_term, and schema mappings
Same workflow steps work across all frameworks with different terminology
Framework-specific analysis enabled (e.g., cycles expected in biological networks)

functional_requirements.requirement: Generate machine-readable architecture artifacts
functional_requirements.description: Create structured architecture files (service_architecture.json, component_architecture.json, etc.) for each system component following framework-specific schemas
acceptance_criteria: Architecture files follow framework-specific JSON schemas
Files include complete component/service definitions
Interface/connection definitions specified with contracts
Version tracking enabled for architecture evolution
functional_requirements.context_consumption: Medium (3000-10000 tokens per architecture file generation)

functional_requirements.requirement: Validate architectural artifacts for completeness and correctness
functional_requirements.description: Run automated validation tools to check architectures for missing elements, inconsistencies, and violations of framework rules
acceptance_criteria: validate_architecture.py checks architecture file completeness
validate_foundational_alignment.py ensures alignment with mission/scenarios
Validation reports list critical, warning, and info issues
Quality gates block workflow progression until critical issues resolved
functional_requirements.context_consumption: Medium (2000-5000 tokens per validation run with output)

functional_requirements.requirement: Analyze system-of-systems graphs for architectural issues
functional_requirements.description: Generate directed graphs of system components/connections and analyze for orphaned nodes, missing edges, cycles, disconnected components, and other architectural problems
acceptance_criteria: system_of_systems_graph_v2.py generates NetworkX graph from architecture files
Graph analysis includes: orphan detection, connectivity analysis, cycle detection, path analysis
Framework-specific analysis (e.g., cycles may be expected in some domains)
Analysis output highlights critical architectural issues
functional_requirements.context_consumption: High (10000-30000 tokens for large system graphs)

functional_requirements.requirement: Generate human-readable documentation from machine-readable architectures
functional_requirements.description: Create Interface Contract Documents (ICDs), Mermaid diagrams, architecture handoff documents, and other human-readable artifacts from structured architecture files
acceptance_criteria: ICDs generated for each service/component interface
Mermaid diagrams visualize system connections
Architecture handoff documents provide human overview
Documentation stays synchronized with architecture files

functional_requirements.requirement: Define and visualize functional architecture before system allocation
functional_requirements.description: Create functional requirements, process flows, and decision flows showing WHAT the system must do before allocating functions to services/components
acceptance_criteria: Functional requirements extracted from foundational documents
Functional architecture defines process flows, decision flows, data flows
Human-readable visualizations (BPMN, UML) generated for stakeholder review
Functional architecture validated for completeness before system decomposition
functional_requirements.context_consumption: High (10000-25000 tokens for functional architecture + visualizations)

functional_requirements.requirement: Analyze functional architecture for gaps and inefficiencies
functional_requirements.description: Use graph analysis on functional architecture to detect missing functions, redundant functions, circular dependencies, and incomplete flows before system allocation
acceptance_criteria: Functional architecture graph generated showing functions and flows
Gap detection identifies missing functions needed to complete user scenarios
Redundancy detection finds duplicate or overlapping functions
Flow efficiency analysis detects circular dependencies and bottlenecks
functional_requirements.context_consumption: Medium (5000-15000 tokens for functional graph analysis)

functional_requirements.requirement: Enable stakeholder review and validation of functional architecture
functional_requirements.description: Generate human-readable visualizations (BPMN process flows, UML diagrams, decision trees) for stakeholder review and collect feedback before proceeding to implementation
acceptance_criteria: BPMN 2.0 process flow diagrams generated
UML 2.5 data flow diagrams generated
Decision tree visualizations generated
Stakeholder feedback captured and incorporated through iterative refinement
Stakeholder sign-off obtained before functional allocation
functional_requirements.context_consumption: Medium (5000-15000 tokens per visualization set + iteration)

functional_requirements.requirement: Allocate functions to services/components with high cohesion and low coupling
functional_requirements.description: Create functional allocation matrix mapping each function from functional architecture to specific services, ensuring well-designed service boundaries
acceptance_criteria: Functional allocation matrix created mapping functions to services
100% functional coverage (all functions allocated)
High cohesion (related functions grouped together)
Low coupling (minimal cross-service dependencies)
Service responsibility statements derived from allocated functions

functional_requirements.requirement: Track and manage AI agent context consumption
functional_requirements.description: Monitor context window usage throughout workflows, detect context exhaustion risks, and trigger context refresh operations when necessary to prevent workflow failures
acceptance_criteria: operations_since_refresh counter tracks context accumulation
Context refresh triggered at configurable threshold (default: 5 operations)
Context health status tracked (healthy, warning, critical)
Context refresh procedure documented and executable
functional_requirements.context_consumption: Low (500-1000 tokens for context management overhead)

functional_requirements.requirement: Analyze workflows for context bottlenecks
functional_requirements.description: Identify workflow paths that consume excessive context (>160k tokens), risking context exhaustion and workflow failure for AI agents
acceptance_criteria: Context consumption tracked for each function/step
Cumulative context calculated along all workflow paths
Paths exceeding usable context (160k) flagged as bottlenecks
Recommendations provided for refactoring high-context functions

functional_requirements.requirement: Auto-detect project approach (top-down vs bottom-up)
functional_requirements.description: Automatically determine if project is greenfield (top-down) or integration of existing components (bottom-up) based on presence of code and architecture artifacts
acceptance_criteria: Detect source code, build files, existing architectures in system directory
Route to top-down workflow (SE-00A → SE-00B → SE-01) if greenfield
Route to bottom-up workflow (BU-01 → BU-02) if existing components found
Detection logic documented and configurable

functional_requirements.requirement: Collect workflow execution metrics for retrospectives
functional_requirements.description: Track workflow execution metrics (operations, validations, failures, rework cycles, time per step) for post-workflow analysis and continuous improvement
acceptance_criteria: Metrics tracked in working_memory.json
Retrospective document generated at workflow completion
Metrics include: total_operations, total_validations, validation_failures, rework_cycles
Time per step tracked for bottleneck identification

functional_requirements.requirement: Support safe updates to existing systems with versioning
functional_requirements.description: Enable feature updates and enhancements to existing architectures using versioned architecture files and impact analysis
acceptance_criteria: Change proposals validated against foundational alignment
Functional architecture updated with change deltas visualized
Service architectures versioned (v1.0.0 → v1.1.0 or v2.0.0)
Breaking changes identified and documented
Delta reports show current vs. proposed architectures

functional_requirements.requirement: Detect missing information and architectural issues
functional_requirements.description: Identify knowledge gaps, undefined interfaces, missing components, and architectural inconsistencies through automated analysis
acceptance_criteria: Missing interfaces detected between connected components
Orphaned components identified (no connections)
Undefined interface contracts flagged
Architectural inconsistencies reported with severity levels

functional_requirements.requirement: Generate operational tests based on functional architecture
functional_requirements.description: Create operational test scenarios derived from functional architecture that validate system capabilities (WHAT the system does) rather than just implementation details (HOW it's built)
acceptance_criteria: Operational tests map to functional requirements
Each user scenario has corresponding operational test
Tests validate functional flows from functional architecture
Test coverage measurable against functional architecture completeness

functional_requirements.requirement: Enable Reflow to analyze itself using its own workflows
functional_requirements.description: Support meta-analysis where Reflow workflows analyze Reflow's own architecture to find issues, inefficiencies, and improvement opportunities
acceptance_criteria: Reflow can treat its own workflows as system components
Workflow dependencies analyzed as system-of-systems graph
Context consumption analyzed across all workflow paths
Architectural issues in Reflow itself detected and reported
functional_requirements.context_consumption: Very High (30000-60000 tokens for full meta-analysis)

functional_requirements.requirement: Ensure workflows completable within AI agent context limits
functional_requirements.description: Design workflows to be executable by AI agents within typical context windows (200k tokens), identifying and addressing context bottlenecks
acceptance_criteria: No workflow path consumes > 160k tokens (80% of 200k window)
Context refresh points identified where paths exceed limits
Alternative lower-context paths documented
Context consumption estimates provided for all workflows

estimated_context_consumption.note: Context consumption estimates critical for FR-020 (AI Agent Feasibility)
context_bottleneck_risks: Large system graphs (>20 components) can consume 30000-50000 tokens
Multiple validation iterations accumulate context rapidly
Complex functional architectures with many visualizations consume 20000-40000 tokens
Meta-analysis of Reflow itself approaches context limits
mitigation_strategies: Context refresh operations at regular intervals
Lazy loading of architecture files (read only when needed)
Summarization of validation results rather than full output
Streaming large file reads rather than loading entirely

next_phase.task: Create functional_architecture.json defining HOW these requirements are achieved through functional flows
next_phase.note: Functional architecture will model process flows, decision flows, and data flows showing how Reflow achieves these 20 functional requirements. Context consumption will be tracked as edge weights.
